sources.entry: Super Productivity - Advanced todo list app with integrated timeboxing and time tracking capabilities. Integrates with Jira, GitHub, GitLab, Redmine and OpenProject. (Source Code) MIT Docker

summary.one_liner: Super Productivity is an open-source, offline-first to-do list, time tracker and daily planner for focused personal work, available on desktop, mobile and in the browser.
summary.what_it_does: The app lets you organize tasks with sub-tasks, projects, tags and color coding, and plan your day on a schedule timeline alongside calendar events. It offers boards such as Kanban and Eisenhower Matrix, plus timeboxing and time tracking that can be exported as time sheets and work summaries. Focus tools include Pomodoro, Flowtime and countdown sessions, a break reminder, and an anti-procrastination feature. The README says it can integrate with issue trackers such as Jira, Trello, GitHub, GitLab, Gitea, OpenProject, Linear, ClickUp, Redmine, Nextcloud Deck and Azure DevOps, and offers basic CalDAV integration. Data can be synced via SuperSync, Dropbox or WebDAV, and the README says no account is required and no data is collected.
use_cases: track time spent on tasks and export time sheets
plan the day with a timeline and calendar
sync tasks from Jira or GitHub into a local planner
organize tasks on Kanban or Eisenhower boards
how_to_run: Open the web app (hosted version) in a browser
Download a desktop or mobile build from the project wiki (see platform-specific notes there)
Run with Docker (details are in the wiki under Development)
notable: Offline-first and privacy-focused, with no account or registration required
Integrations with many issue trackers (Jira, GitHub, GitLab, Redmine, OpenProject and others)
Built-in Pomodoro, Flowtime and countdown focus modes with timeboxing
Optional end-to-end encrypted SuperSync service that can be self-hosted
caveats: The web version has limitations compared with the desktop app, per the README's comparison page
Platform downloads and install details are kept in the external wiki rather than the README
The README does not name a Docker image or the exact Docker setup steps
